method: Manual topic/aspect review of independently authored evidence. Sources are grouped by publisher, syndicated copies count once, and amenities are separated from subjective impressions. Labels describe supported amenities and land uses, not residents, safety, noise measurements or a sentiment score. Editorial anchors identify a corridor or area without claiming precise boundaries. No model calls occur at runtime. Broad labels summarise the same reviewed area at wider zoom; district labels add specificity.

sftravel_mission.title: SF Travel: Mission District
sftravel_mission.evidence_note: Names Mission restaurants and shops, Valencia cafes and bars, and 24th Street food businesses. Tourism framing is promotional, so superlatives are excluded.

calle24.title: Calle 24 cultural district
calle24.evidence_note: District organisation publishes separate dining, shopping and cultural assets directories. Supports cultural amenities, not resident demographics.

axios_calle24.title: Axios: Calle 24 food and arts
axios_calle24.evidence_note: Reports on murals, bakeries, cultural shops and a local bookstore. Used as corroboration for the 24th Street corridor.

sftravel_northbeach.title: SF Travel: North Beach
sftravel_northbeach.evidence_note: Identifies cafes, City Lights bookshop and Broadway bars. Promotional tone is excluded from the summary.

ap_northbeach.title: Associated Press: Bay Area places to visit
ap_northbeach.evidence_note: Names North Beach Italian restaurants and City Lights. Only stable amenity types are retained; no ranking or tourist endorsement is reproduced.

sftravel_haight.title: SF Travel: Haight-Ashbury
sftravel_haight.evidence_note: Supports the commercial Haight Street corridor with boutiques and restaurants. Historical counterculture is context, not a label for present residents.

axios_records.title: Axios: San Francisco record shops
axios_records.evidence_note: Identifies Amoeba in Upper Haight, and record shops in the Mission, North Beach, Sunset and Richmond. Used only to corroborate music retail.

sftravel_chinatown.title: SF Travel: Chinatown
sftravel_chinatown.evidence_note: Documents tea rooms, dim sum, cultural institutions and neighbourhood walks. No claims about ethnicity of individual residents are inferred.

chinatown_bakeries.title: Chinatown Volunteer Coalition: bakeries
chinatown_bakeries.evidence_note: Community directory lists multiple bakeries including Stockton-area establishments; supports food and bakery amenities without a quality ranking.

sftravel_sunset.title: SF Travel: Outer Sunset
sftravel_sunset.evidence_note: Describes Ocean Beach, cafes and local shops. Claims about tranquillity are not used as measured noise evidence.

aaa_sunset.title: AAA Via: exploring the Sunset
aaa_sunset.evidence_note: Corroborates the beach, residential grid and neighbourhood cafe/retail amenities. Membership travel editorial may favour visitor attractions.

sftravel_dogpatch.title: SF Travel: Dogpatch and Mission Bay
sftravel_dogpatch.evidence_note: Documents former shipyard context, waterfront parks and dining. Promotional impressions such as sleepy or welcoming are omitted.

sfplanning_waterfront.title: SF Planning: Central Waterfront plan
sfplanning_waterfront.evidence_note: Documents industrial heritage, Dogpatch residential core and mixed waterfront uses. A plan records policy and historic context, not proof all proposed amenities were completed.

daly_legacy.title: Daly City: legacy business registry
daly_legacy.evidence_note: Lists Fil-Am Cuisine at School Street and other legacy businesses along Mission. Business descriptions are promotional; only presence and category are used.

kqed_daly.title: KQED: Daly City food history
kqed_daly.evidence_note: Reports on Filipino food businesses including Fil-Am Cuisine and local bakeries. Historic reporting corroborates the food tradition; it is not used for current business hours.

brisbane_park.title: Brisbane: Community Park
brisbane_park.evidence_note: Official listing places Community Park at the town centre with playground and picnic facilities. Review used indexed official content; direct fetch timed out.

sfgate_brisbane.title: SFGATE: Visitacion Avenue
sfgate_brisbane.evidence_note: Corroborates Visitacion Avenue commercial corridor and Community Park. Old named businesses are not assumed still open; current park listing supports the enduring place feature.

ssf_walk.title: South San Francisco: downtown walking tours
ssf_walk.evidence_note: Documents Grand Avenue downtown historic sites and self-guided walks. Supports historic main-street character, not every business being historic.

chronicle_ssf.title: Chronicle: South San Francisco main street
chronicle_ssf.evidence_note: Reports Grand Avenue as the downtown commercial spine. Older article supports enduring urban form; named restaurants are not treated as current.

ssf_east101.title: Shape SSF: East of 101
ssf_east101.evidence_note: Identifies biotechnology campuses and waterfront access in East of 101. Proposed improvements are not reported as completed.

kqed_ssf.title: KQED: South San Francisco biotechnology
kqed_ssf.evidence_note: Independent history and present-day account of the city's biotechnology industry, updated October 2026. Supports district land use, not employment forecasts.

sanbruno_plan.title: San Bruno: San Mateo Avenue streetscape plan
sanbruno_plan.evidence_note: Identifies San Mateo Avenue as downtown main street with restaurant/retail uses. Proposed streetscape works are not assumed complete.

localnews_sanbruno.title: Local News Matters: San Bruno walking tours
localnews_sanbruno.evidence_note: Reports downtown shops, restaurants and older buildings along San Mateo Avenue. Syndicated copies of this article would count as the same source.

areas.explanation: The 24th Street corridor combines murals, food businesses and cultural shops. These are documented amenities, rather than a description of every street or its residents.
areas.limitations: Selective corridor summary. Tourism and district sources promote local businesses; opening hours and perceived street activity vary.

areas.explanation: Valencia Street has mapped cafes and bars alongside clothing shops and music retail. This describes the commercial corridor and makes no claim about measured noise or nightlife attendance.
areas.limitations: Street-level character changes by block and time. No street-activity or noise measurement is asserted.

areas.explanation: Columbus Avenue and nearby streets combine Italian dining, cafes and literary landmarks such as City Lights. Broadway's bars are nearby; the label is an amenity summary.
areas.limitations: Not all establishments are Italian or literary. Tourism and event-focused reporting do not establish uniform conditions or opening hours.

areas.explanation: The Haight Street commercial corridor includes record retail and boutiques, with restaurants between them. Its music history is context, not a label for today's residents.
areas.limitations: Retail changes over time; the label identifies a corridor and does not imply every shop is independent or vintage.

areas.explanation: Chinatown offers bakeries, tea rooms and dim sum venues alongside cultural institutions. The label concerns food and amenities, without inferring anyone's ethnicity from location or business names.
areas.limitations: Community and tourism directories are selective and may lag changes. The label does not cover every establishment.

areas.explanation: The western Sunset meets Ocean Beach, with residential streets and cafe/retail corridors nearby. Beach and park access are documented; tranquillity or noise is not measured.
areas.limitations: Broad land-use summary. Weather, street conditions and activity vary. Independent travel editorial also favours visitor amenities.

areas.explanation: Dogpatch combines industrial heritage and reused buildings with waterfront parks and food businesses. The district is mixed; industrial and residential uses both remain.
areas.limitations: Planning documents include proposals, so only established uses and described heritage inform the label. No uniform transformation is claimed.

areas.area_name: Daly City, Mission and School Street
areas.explanation: The Mission Street area includes documented Filipino food businesses and bakeries, including a city-listed legacy restaurant at School Street. This describes food amenities and local urban form.
areas.evidence_strength: Official registry and independent food reporting
areas.limitations: KQED's food history is older; named current business evidence comes from the city registry. This is selective coverage, not a citywide dining census.

areas.explanation: Visitacion Avenue forms a small commercial corridor by Community Park, below the hillside residential streets. The park and corridor are enduring features described by city information and local reporting.
areas.evidence_strength: Corroborated physical features, limited recent reporting
areas.limitations: The independent street guide dates from 2010. Its named businesses are not assumed open; current official park information was reviewed through indexed content after a fetch timeout.

areas.explanation: Grand Avenue is the downtown commercial spine, with local eateries and documented historic buildings. A self-guided city walking tour explains the area's heritage.
areas.limitations: Independent reporting is historical and does not verify current individual eateries. The label describes the corridor rather than all of South San Francisco.

areas.explanation: East of Highway 101 has a substantial biotechnology and office-campus presence near the bay. Public waterfront routes provide a different context from the downtown Grand Avenue corridor.
areas.evidence_strength: Official land-use account and independent journalism
areas.limitations: Campus access and public paths are different. Planning proposals are not assumed built; this label does not imply residential availability or public access to private campuses.

areas.explanation: San Mateo Avenue is San Bruno's downtown main street, with restaurants, shops and older low-rise buildings documented in local reporting and the city streetscape plan.
areas.evidence_strength: Official plan and independent local reporting
areas.limitations: The plan includes proposed works, not proof they are complete. Business names, hours and perceptions of activity may change.

research_queue.reason: Requires independent current evidence for a narrower amenity summary; citywide food reporting should not be relocated here.
Current mixed land-use and public-space evidence should be gathered before publishing a character label.
Insufficient independent place-specific evidence in this review; no invented label fills the gap.
Downtown evidence does not support claims about hillside districts.
Only part of Pacifica lies inside this project's study bounds; verify corridor anchors and sources before adding labels.
Coverage is deliberately selective. Additional labels need independent corroboration and a separate review.
